name: Advent Trail
tag: The Advent Post: telephone in three huts along a lantern trail

chain.has: sees 3 of the 5 pictures
sees the other 2, merges all 5 into day order
12 tiles and the calendar board

win: Hang the 5 right tiles, from 12, in day order and press check.
cost: Seven and a half minutes and three strikes. Then the doors open, the displays blank and new pictures are dealt.
own: The middle player holds part of the answer and has to merge two halves into one order.
lobby: Four: a second listening chair adds a link. Two: a memory trip between the huts.

plan.idea: The Calendar House shows today's five pictures in day order. Their tiles wait at five far places, named by landmark and coordinates. Fetch them by rail, mine or on foot and hang them in order.

name: Bauble Hunt
tag: Bauble Wood: blank baubles only a telescope can read

chain.has: display of the 3 baubles wanted; hangs what arrives
ink telescope shows the pictures on 16 baubles
sees every bauble blank; carries them to the posting box, in order

win: The 3 right baubles on the board (5 with four players), checked while one player holds a button in the Hut, one on the tower and one in the wood.
cost: A wrong check stops the puzzle and deals new baubles. No clock.
own: Eight designs made from three either-or features, so every design has three near-twins. The fetcher cannot see what they fetch.
lobby: Four: five designs and two Hunters. Two: three round trips, 20 to 30 minutes.

plan.idea: The hut comes down. The wanted baubles show on a board in the open, one player reads the blank baubles through the ink telescope, and the rest fetch and hang them. No hold, no lock-in.

name: Bell Ringers
tag: Call Changes: six bell mats in a belfry of two rooms

chain.has: lamp map of both ringing rooms

chain.at: one in each room, a wall between
chain.has: six coloured mats; the tenor's mat spans the wall

win: 12 calls in a row, 5 s each: the called mat occupied and no other. The tenor counts only with both ringers on it. Then everyone pulls a lever within the same second.
cost: One wrong call and the peal starts again. A failed finale costs the whole peal.
own: One target needs two people who cannot see each other. Voices are not guarded here: bodies and timing are the lock.
lobby: Four: 14 calls. Two: 10 calls of 6 s.

plan.idea: The belfry rings a peal, lamp by lamp. Ring it back from memory on the six mats; each round adds a bell. The tenor still needs two ringers. A slip repeats the round.

name: Big Air
tag: A ski-jump final judged from a sealed cabin

chain.has: three coloured lamps

chain.via: one-way intercom, 90 m up the run

chain.has: three kickers: red, green, gold

win: 6 clean calls inside 5 minutes: take the kicker of the lit colour and fly through its window, 6 m above the landing.
cost: A wrong window fails the whole run, and every try costs a hike of about 120 m back up.
own: The only puzzle judged in the air. The riders take turns and must never both fly on one call.
lobby: Four: 8 calls. Two: 4 calls.

plan.idea: The lit colour shows at the start hut. Fly through that kicker's window, three times. No judge and no clock.

chain.at: start hut 90 m up the run, on skis
chain.has: three kickers (red, green, gold), each with a window 6 m over its landing

now.win: Fly through each of the three windows once, in any order. A lamp over each window lights when it is done.
now.cost: Nothing but the walk back up.
now.own: Skill on skis alone: hold enough speed onto a 3.5 m kicker to reach its window.
now.lobby: Any number can ride; a window counts whoever flies it.

name: Blind Carols
tag: The Carol Chapel: tunes passed on by humming to blind hands

chain.has: hears one carol and nothing else; hums it
hears the tile held up in the window niche
nine identical speaking tiles and the coloured slots

win: Hang the right tune in each carol's slot: 4 carols from 9 tunes (5 with four players).
cost: A 10-minute clock stops the puzzle and deals the carols again. So does anyone passing a vestry gate.
own: The answer is a sound, it travels as a hum, and the hands that hang it cannot see.
lobby: Four: two Listeners on one Guide. Two: slower, mostly memory.

plan.idea: The carols play from the bell cotes in the open. A blindfolded player in the vestry finds each tune among the tiles by ear, and friends at the window say which slot is which colour. No headphones, no clock.

name: Blind Sculptor
tag: The Snow Sculptor's Court: invisible ink and a blindfold

chain.at: kiosk facing away from the court
chain.has: the commission: 5 pictures
ink telescope shows the 12 tiles' pictures
tiles in racks, a five-slot board, the check button

win: The 5 right tiles, from 12, on the plinth's board. The sculptor presses check.
cost: An 8-minute clock. Two wrong checks stop the puzzle and deal a new commission.
own: Ink and blindfold together: the one who can see the pictures has no hands in the court, and the hands have no eyes.
lobby: Four: a second patron and an ordering problem. Two: 25 to 40 minutes by memory.

plan.idea: The commission hangs where the guides can see it and the tiles show their pictures. The blindfolded sculptor is talked to each tile and slot from the wall. No telescope, no clock, no strikes.

name: Blizzard Walk
tag: A snow maze steered from a crow's nest, called from 300 m away

chain.has: a map of the 12 alcove lamps, without the maze's walls

chain.at: crow's nest 14 m over the maze, seated
chain.has: sees the maze and the walker

chain.at: in a 21 m maze of 2.6 m walls
chain.has: sighted, on foot

win: 6 phases in a row, 22 s each: stand in the lit dead-end alcove with nobody in any other. (8 with four players.)
cost: One miss empties the bar and the run starts again.
own: The caller is out of sight and earshot of the whole site, and each route is run at speed.
lobby: Four: a second Walker. Two: the Walker works from memory, 20 to 35 minutes.

plan.idea: No signal hut. Anyone can climb the crow's nest, see which alcove is lit and steer the walkers to its button. Five alcoves and no phase timer.

name: Downhill
tag: The Called Slalom, one skier: a giant slalom called by two huts

chain.at: timing hut at the finish; start house at the lift's top
chain.has: lamps for rows 1 to 3; lamps for rows 4 to 6
six rows of red, green and blue gates

win: Pass the live gate of each of 6 rows, then put the timer ball in the holder at the finish before the clock runs out.
cost: One wrong gate kills the run, and the way back up is a 95 s lift ride.
own: Each row is shown only on a panel the skier has already left or not yet reached, so the call is handed from one hut to the other mid-run.
lobby: Four: a third hut on the cat track. Two: not promised.

plan.idea: A pack run: each row's lit gate shows on the gate itself and counts only with the whole group through it together. No callers, no ball, no clock.

name: Fairy Lights
tag: The Lamplighter's Glade: pads known only by their picture

chain.has: lamps, each under a scribble

chain.via: one-way intercom to speakers at every station

chain.has: two pads each, a scribble hanging over each

win: 10 rounds in a row at 7.5 s: the runner who owns the named picture stands on its pad, nobody on any other. On the gold star lamp, every runner stands in the Star Ring.
cost: One wrong phase stops the puzzle. The next start deals new pictures and a new shuffle.
own: Which pad a lamp means is reshuffled on every start, so the picture is the only address. The star call gathers everyone in one ring.
lobby: Four: a third station.

plan.idea: A lights-out puzzle: each lamp post's button flips its own string of lights and its neighbours'. Light the whole glade.

name: Footprints
tag: The Signal Field: sixteen pads hidden under the snow

chain.has: the lamp board
sees the field
pads they cannot see; row and column stakes

win: 10 pads in a row, 9 s each: stand on the lit pad and on no other.
cost: One miss and the run starts again.
own: The pads are invisible. The Walker lines up coloured row stakes and banded column stakes, and their own tracks in the snow are the only trace.
lobby: Four: a fence splits the field between two Walkers. Two: no soundproofing, walkie-talkies supplied.

plan.idea: The lamp board stands in the open at the field's edge. Find the lit pad from its row and column stakes without treading on another. Six pads, no timer.

now.tag: Find the lit pad from its two stakes

chain.has: sixteen pads hidden under the snow; a tall lamp board over the cab shows which one is lit

now.win: Six lit pads found. Stand on the lit pad for a moment and it counts.
now.cost: Nothing: there is no clock and treading on other pads is free.
now.own: The pads are invisible. Row stakes give the colour, column stakes the number of bands, and your own tracks show where you have been.
now.lobby: With more players, one on the cab's platform sees the whole field and can call the walkers on.

name: Glass Booth
tag: A relay whose first link has no words

chain.has: a five-flap display

chain.at: outside, at a rack of 12 tiles
chain.has: takes the tiles pointed at
a five-slot board whose slots are labelled in dots

win: 5 tiles, from 12, in the right slots inside 4 minutes.
cost: A wrong check ends the round, the display deals again and every tile goes back to the rack.
own: No speech at all on the first link. The order key is split: only the Keeper sees the slot labels, only the Reader the matching dots.
lobby: Four: a second Spotter. Two: one player is Spotter and Keeper.

plan.idea: Stays as it is: one of the five that keep their sealed rooms.

name: Hold the Star
tag: Hold buttons called from a soundproof chamber under a great fir

chain.has: lamp map: three colours for each station

chain.at: stations 22 m out in the snow
chain.has: red, green and gold hold buttons

win: 10 rounds in a row, 5 s each: the right holder holds the right colour and nobody holds anything else. Then the Reader runs out and everyone holds a star button for 6 unbroken seconds.
cost: Any slip throws away the whole count.
own: Letting go on time matters as much as holding. The finale brings the caller out to hold with the rest.
lobby: Four: a third station and 12 rounds. Two: about 8 minutes.

plan.idea: Hold buttons spread round the fir, one of them out of a single player's reach, light the star and open the box while all are held. One player more than the buttons takes the gourd. A short, gentle one.

name: Light the Tree
tag: The Lantern Ring: everyone watches a neighbour's lamps

chain.at: an open shelter, 18 m from the tree
chain.has: two hold buttons under pictures; the lamps of the next shelter's buttons
the same: nobody can see their own lamps

win: 12 rounds in a row, 5 s each: the owner of the lit lantern holds its button and nobody holds another.
cost: One wrong or missing hold stops the puzzle. New pictures are dealt and the lamps re-hung.
own: No caller and no doer: all three do both jobs at once, and nobody is shut in.
lobby: Two: two shelters.

plan.idea: The lantern ring stays, without the 5 s phases: a lantern stays lit until its owner presses. Eight in a row.

name: Lookouts
tag: An island-wide signal relay against the clock

chain.has: one display each
12 scribble tiles; slots keyed by colour and pips

win: Fill the board, then everyone pulls a lever within the same 2 seconds.
cost: A 4-minute timer and three strikes. Then the displays blank and new pictures are dealt.
own: The only puzzle that uses the island's size: players reach their posts by train, mine or gondola before the first start.
lobby: Four: a third beacon at the summit. Two: 10 to 15 minutes.

plan.idea: Stays as it is: apart by distance, not by walls, with two-way radio.

name: Midnight Finale
tag: The island's fireworks show, fired by its crew

chain.has: lamps beside scribbles; the units change places every start
three hold buttons each, a scribble over each

win: 12 calls in a row, 5 s each. Then, within 15 s, everyone pulls a lever inside the same 1.5 s and the rockets go up.
cost: A misfire anywhere restarts the show from the top.
own: It ends in real fireworks, seen across the island.
lobby: Four: a third bay and nine scribbles.

plan.idea: Stays as it is: the finale, and the one timed-hold relay left.

name: Radio Silence
tag: A signal station of sealed rooms along the ravine

chain.at: sealed hut on the ravine floor
chain.has: 3 pictures

chain.at: sealed booth on the ravine's lip
chain.has: 2 more pictures; merges all 5, in order
10 scribble tiles and a five-slot board

win: 5 scribbles, from 10, in order inside 5 minutes.
cost: A wrong check ends the round, opens every door and deals again. So does leaving a sealed room.
own: The only way back up the line is a button that lights a lamp in the room before, so the group has to invent a signal code.
lobby: Four: a Lookout with a sixth picture also talks into the Relay's headphones.

plan.idea: Stays as it is: one of the five that keep their sealed rooms.

name: Reindeer Count
tag: Roll Call in the Reindeer Shed: twenty stalls, no place sees them all

chain.at: galleries outside the shed's west and east windows
chain.has: each sees only the stalls that face them

chain.at: shut in the windowless Tally Barn
chain.has: a floor plan of the shed with a pad at every stall

win: 13 in a row, 7 s each: stand on the pad of the stall whose nose lamp lit, and on no other. (15 with four players, 10 with two.)
cost: One miss empties the bar.
own: The usual arrangement reversed: the one shut in is the doer. The galleries face each other, so one spotter's left is the other's right, and the first question is who can see the lamp at all.
lobby: Four: a north gallery. Two: 10 in a row.

plan.idea: Back to counting: some noses light at each start, each gallery sees only part of the shed, and the views overlap. Agree the number and enter it. A wrong count deals again.

name: Santa's List
tag: Two lists that reach the packer by two senses

chain.at: keyhole telescope, down a 31 m hall
chain.has: reads the Nice List
the Toy Shelf's tiles and a six-slot board
the Naughty List; cannot speak to anyone

win: 6 tiles in slots keyed by list and flap. Then everyone pulls a sleigh-bell lever within 3 seconds.
cost: A 5-minute clock and three wrong checks. Then both lists blank and the booth opens.
own: Two sources reach one player at the same time, one spoken and one mimed.
lobby: Four: a second booth. Two: no Lookout.

plan.idea: Checking it twice: the two lists hang at opposite ends of the yard and differ in two places. Call them across and mark the two that differ.

name: Slalom
tag: The Called Slalom, a pair: two skiers through the same lane together

chain.has: lamp map of the course

chain.via: intercom to speakers along the course, or walkie-talkies

chain.has: six rows of three coloured lanes

win: Every row: both skiers inside the live lane at once, each row within its own clock of 6 to 8 s.
cost: A wrong lane or a late row ends the run, and it is a walk back up.
own: The pair must arrive together, and a row's lane is only chosen when the row before is passed.
lobby: Two: a 15 to 25 minute race.

plan.idea: A reaction slalom for one skier: the next row's live lane lights on its own gate as the last is passed. Six rows clean.

now.tag: A reaction slalom for one skier

chain.has: six rows of three coloured lanes; the next row's live lane lights on its own gate as the last is passed

now.win: Ski the lit lane of all six rows in one run, then the finish arch.
now.cost: A wrong lane, or skiing past a row, ends the run. Going through the start arch again deals a new one. No clock.
now.own: The lane to take is only known one row ahead.
now.lobby: One run at a time: a second skier through the start arch restarts it.

name: Sleigh Run
tag: The Sleigh Shed: carry the present through doors only others can open

chain.at: inside a soundproof, radio-dead snow shed
chain.has: carries the present; sees two scribbles over each door
tiles and a peg board for each door

win: Carry the present (the game's timer ball) through 3 doors to the sleigh before its clock runs out. A door opens only while its two scribbles hang on its board.
cost: The present goes back to the workshop and the runner walks out. Each door can be used once.
own: The one doing the carrying is also the one describing. The only answer they ever get is a door swinging open.
lobby: Two: two doors. Four: four doors.

plan.idea: The present is the timer ball: it lasts ten seconds and the shed is too long for one runner, so it is thrown from chamber to chamber through hatches. The one puzzle that is a race.

name: Snow Bridge
tag: The Survey Party: two boards of invisible-ink tiles across two gullies

chain.has: reads the two displays
ink telescope shows the tiles' pictures
blank tiles and two peg boards

win: Board A right uncovers the load-test button and the second display. Board B is judged by holding buttons at the cairn, on the pier and in the gully at once.
cost: A failed load test stops the puzzle and deals both displays again. No clock.
own: Two boards one after the other, with the work moving across the gullies between them. No walls and no clock: voices are free.
lobby: Two: 35 to 50 minutes. Four: a winch.

plan.idea: Build it: carry snow blocks from the banks and set them in the gaps; each span appears when its blocks are in. Some blocks lie beyond the first span.

name: Snow Globe
tag: A keeper sealed in a glass dome who can only mime back

chain.has: pictures at the end of a 12 m tunnel
the only intercom into the globe

chain.via: intercom in; gestures back through the glass

chain.has: 8 winter scribbles and a peg board

win: 5 scribbles on the board inside 7 minutes.
cost: The clock stops the puzzle and deals new pictures.
own: The Keeper is in plain view of everyone and cannot say a word, so questions come back as mime. It has a picture sheet of its own.
lobby: Four: a second shed and six pictures.

plan.idea: Stays as it is: one of the five that keep their sealed rooms.

name: Snowball Range
tag: A thrower who never sees the target

chain.has: lamps beside the hoops' pictures; the cells change places
sees the six hoops and where every ball goes
lobs through a curtained chute

win: 6 hits with 18 snowballs inside 6 minutes.
cost: A ball through the wrong hoop ends the run.
own: Aim by words alone, at hoops 7 to 16 m off and at different heights. The roles are split by sight, so radios change nothing.

plan.idea: An open range: a lamp lights on one hoop, put a snowball through it, six times. Everyone can see the hoops.

now.tag: An open range of six baskets on poles

chain.at: wherever they like on the range
chain.has: twelve snowballs from the bin; six baskets with rims 3.0 to 3.6 m up

now.win: A snowball into each of the six baskets, in any order. A basket's lamp lights when it is hit.
now.cost: Nothing. A miss lies on the snow to pick up again, and a ball that lands in a basket is laid back in the bin.
now.own: The base game's basketball, six times over at different heights. How far players can throw was not measured: the heights follow the base game's own hoop.
now.lobby: Any number can throw at once.

name: Snowman
tag: The Snowman Contest: move the whole snowman to the plot that is called

chain.at: shut in the windowless Judges' Box
chain.has: six lamps beside copies of six faces
three snowballs; six plots, each under a faceless head wearing a picture

win: 8 judgings in a row, 21 s each: all three snowballs set down in the plot whose head wears the lit face. (10 with four players.)
cost: Any miss stops the contest and the next start deals new faces.
own: Each press is a load: three snowballs, one per pair of hands, up to 14 m.
lobby: Four: 10 in a row. Two: hard, if at all.

plan.idea: Nine snowballs of three sizes lie round the fort, some out of easy reach. Build three whole snowmen in the three plots.

name: Stocking Sort
tag: Christmas Eve at the Lakeside Cottage: presents down the chimney

chain.has: three children's wishes

chain.via: heard only in the Wrapper's headphones

chain.has: eight wrapped presents; sits to listen, stands to talk

chain.via: down the chimney chute, saying whose it is

chain.has: the other two wishes; five stockings by emblem

win: 5 presents, from 8, in the right stockings (6 with four players), checked while one player holds a button in each of the three rooms.
cost: An 8-minute clock. A wrong check stops the puzzle and deals new wishes.
own: A hub that sees neither list. Any two presents differ in at least two of four features, so a short description fits two of them.
lobby: Four: six stockings and three voices in one pair of headphones. Two: 15 to 25 minutes.

plan.idea: A deduction: the right order of five presents is hidden. Hang a guess and the mantel's lamps show how many stockings are right, not which.

name: Summit Shot
tag: The Lob House: a blind lob over a wall, on the summit

chain.has: lamp panel beside the baskets' shapes; the lamps change places

chain.via: intercom, heard only on the deck

chain.has: sees the baskets and every landing
snowballs; a 3.3 m wall in front

win: 8 baskets in a row before the clock runs out (10 with four players).
cost: A ball in the wrong basket empties the streak. Misses are free: the balls roll back to the thrower.
own: A blind lob into a 0.84 m basket. Missing costs nothing, which no other streak puzzle allows.
lobby: Four: a second caller with half the lamps. Two: the lamps move to the spotter's deck.

plan.idea: For two: the thrower cannot see the baskets over the wall, the spotter on the deck can, and they simply talk. No blindfold, no hut, no clock. Eight baskets; a wrong one costs one.

name: Thin Ice
tag: A blind crossing of a frozen pond with open water in it

chain.has: lamp map of the pond
sees the pond; hears only the spotter
25 floes in a grid, five of them open water

win: 10 floes in a row, 17 s each: stand on the lit floe with nobody on any other (8 with four players).
cost: Any miss, or a fall into a hole, resets the count to zero.
own: Holes on the route: the straight line is often the wrong one, and the walker cannot see it.
lobby: Four: two spotters with half a map each. Two: one link fewer, 15 s.

plan.idea: For two: the map hangs on the watch tower. One reads it and talks the blindfolded crosser to the lit floe, round the holes. Six floes, no phase timer.

now.tag: For two: a guide on the tower and a blindfolded crosser

chain.has: a lamp map of the floes on the wall behind them; sees the pond
25 floes in a grid, five of them open water

now.win: Six lit floes reached, one at a time. Stand on the lit floe for a moment and it counts.
now.cost: Nothing: stepping on other floes is free, and a fall into a hole only costs the climb out. No clock.
now.own: The ice is for the blindfolded only: anyone on it without the blindfold is set back outside. So it takes two.
now.lobby: More players can share the guiding or take turns on the ice.

name: Whispering Chimney
tag: Tunes heard down four chimneys, matched by humming both ways

chain.has: each hears one chimney's tune; hums it
compares two hums and gives the verdict
nine speaking tiles; hums candidates back

win: 3 tunes hung in chimney order (4 with four players), then poke the validator.
cost: A wrong answer stops the puzzle and the next start deals new tunes. No clock.
own: The one line that runs both ways: candidates are hummed back and the relay judges two hums, neither of them the real tune. No clock.
lobby: Four: a fourth chimney.

plan.idea: Each chimney's tune can be heard at its own hearth. Match the tiles by ear and hang them in chimney order. No chairs and no relay.

name: Whiteout Maze
tag: A blindfolded walker talked through a maze where a wrong turn ends it

chain.has: lamp board with a picture beside each lamp
sees the pictures lying face-up over 8 cairns, and the walker
walls too tall to see over

win: 6 cairns before the clock runs out.
cost: Stepping into the wrong dead end stops the puzzle.
own: A wrong turn is fatal, not just slow. The lamp board is shuttered unless someone stands on the gantry.
lobby: Four: two blind walkers must reach each cairn together.

plan.idea: A maze of gates: standing on a plate opens a gate somewhere else, so the group leapfrogs to the middle. No blindfold, no clock.
